title: Building a central AI team that becomes everyone’s bottleneck
summary: Centralise reusable support and essential controls while keeping local outcomes and workflow knowledge close to the work.
diagnosis: Central expertise is valuable, but a central team asked to discover, build, approve and support every use case becomes a queue. Unrestricted decentralisation creates a different problem: duplicated integrations, inconsistent controls and unowned applications. Distinguish shared capabilities from local delivery decisions, and make the route for obtaining help explicit.
diagnostic_questions: Which requests genuinely need specialist central work, and which are waiting for permission or reusable components?
Can business teams build within a supported path without bypassing controls?
Who maintains shared context, evaluation tools and integrations after the first team benefits?
proposed_actions: Publish a central service catalog with supported platforms, reusable patterns, review services, escalation routes and response expectations.
Delegate bounded decisions to trained local owners; keep non-negotiable identity, data and release controls common.
Fund maintenance of shared capabilities and recurring knowledge exchange, not only the visible backlog of new prototypes.
working_artifact: Federated operating model: central services; local responsibilities; approved building paths; required review gates; support capacity; reusable component owners; exception process; knowledge-sharing cadence.
measures: Request lead time by category and proportion resolved through supported self-service.
Reuse of maintained components, with duplication and support burden measured rather than assumed away.
Rate of unsupported deployments and unresolved ownership gaps, interpreted without punishing honest reporting.
tradeoff: Federation is not a reason to distribute specialist security or reliability decisions to unprepared teams. Equally, a centre of excellence should not become the exclusive owner of business knowledge. Organisational size and risk may justify different degrees of centralisation.
illustrative_case: Illustrative application: the central team provides identity, connectors and evaluation tooling; a finance process owner supplies reconciliation rules and acceptance cases. Shared support accelerates local delivery without transferring all finance judgement to the platform team.
